title: Population-based cohort study for digital health research in Germany
summary:
The DigiHero study was launched in January 2021 by institutes and clinics at Halle (Saale) University Hospital. The aim of the study is to investigate various health topics using digital methods. The initial focus was particularly on research into SARS-CoV-2 and the consequences of the pandemic. This led to further investigations into Long/Post-COVID and other post-acute infection syndromes (PAIS) emerging as new key research priorities. Other topics include the development of chronic diseases, healthy ageing and public health in general. 
The study was launched in Halle (Saale). Thanks to funding from the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Science and Digitalisation of the State of Saxony-Anhalt, the study was expanded to include further districts in Saxony-Anhalt. Recruitment took place across the whole of Central Germany (Saxony-Anhalt, Saxony and Thuringia). The study has since been extended to cover the whole of Germany through recruitment in selected regions across all German federal states.
External funding has already been secured from various funding bodies (e.g. the Federal Ministry of Health, the Federal Ministry of Federal Affairs, Transport and Telecommunications) to investigate specific research questions using data from the DigiHero study.  
The DigiHero study was initiated by four institutes and six clinical departments at Halle (Saale) University Hospital. Furthermore, as part of a federated approach, the following project sites joined the study with their own research teams: Jena University Hospital; the Leibniz ScienceCampus Digital Public Health (LSC DiPH) in Bremen, represented by the Leibniz Institute for Prevention Research and Epidemiology – BIPS and the University of Bremen; the Institute for Prevention and Occupational Medicine of the German Social Accident Insurance, an institute of Ruhr University (IPA) in Bochum; the Institute for Epidemiology and Social Medicine at the University of Münster; the Department of Public Health at the Brandenburg University of Technology Cottbus-Senftenberg; and the Department of Psychiatry and Neurosciences at the Benjamin Franklin Campus of Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin.
